rationale: Lycopolitan ⲥⲁⲓⲱ likely = Sah. ⲥⲁⲓⲏ/ⲥⲁⲏ 'beam, log, post' (Crum 372a). In context of the Enemy as the structure on which sinners are 'crucified' (line 4-5), the beam-of-the-Enemy = the eschatological stake/gallows. Tentative.

Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲣ̄-ⲭⲁⲣⲉ where ⲭⲁⲣⲉ likely = Greek χήρα 'widow,' Lycopolitan-orthographized. 'State-of-being-widowed' = desolation, destitution. Eschatological state of the sinners bound in the bōlos. Tentative.

proposed_english: to sojourn / to dwell as stranger
rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of ⲣ̄-ϣⲙ̄ⲙⲟ 'be a stranger, sojourn' (with ⲗ for ⲙ). Fits the image of the damned as foreigners assigned to the bōlos as their last dwelling. Tentative.
Possibly Greek ζωπύριον 'live-coal' or related Greek loan denoting an enclosure of fire/filth. One of three identifications of the bōlos. Confidence low.
Reduplicated form, possibly Lycopolitan ϣⲁⲡϣⲡ̄ 'gloom, dimness, twilight.' Triple-paired with 'ember-pit' and 'shadow' as identifications of the bōlos.
Possibly privative ⲁⲧ-ⲏⲡⲉ 'without count/number.' Modifies ⲍⲁⲃⲥ 'shadow' as the eternal-darkness attribute of the bōlos. Alternative: ⲁⲧ-ⲉⲓⲃⲉ 'without thirst.' Tentative.
Lyc. ⲧⲁⲱ likely = ⲧⲱϣ/ⲧⲁϣ 'boundary, limit.' The bōlos-stone as the absolute boundary-marker between Light and Darkness.
Lyc. ⲧⲱϩ/ⲧⲱϩⲥ̄ 'strike, smite' — the verb governing ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ in this kephalaion's 'three plagues that strike the Enemy.' Three attestations on this page (lines 12, 17, 30).

Verbal noun, possibly ⲣⲁ- (intensifying prefix) + ⲟⲩⲱⲗ/ⲱⲗ 'carry, lift.' The eschatological act constituting the Third Plague: the cosmic carrying-off and final separation of all things at the end. Confidence low — flag for parallels.
ⲍⲁⲉ = Lyc. ϩⲁⲉ 'last, final.' Standard Manichaean eschatological term: the Last Bōlos = the final dark mass into which residual matter and damned souls are sealed. Cf. accumulated entry ⲡⲃⲱⲗⲟⲥ.
